doc.title: Oliver Nelson Jr. interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, September 10, 2020

title: Faith, the turbulent year and politics
summary: His Bible-based view of 2020, anger at evangelical politics, and hope in diverse protests and young voters.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Politics, race and the state of the country

blocks.x: We are in the midst of a historically turbulent year in so many ways. Are you a spiritual man?
Do you have any thoughts about why all this is occurring now?

I think, and I’m just going to go from my Bible reading and that kind of stuff that I do a lot. The Bible talks about these kinds of things happening. But I’ve never seen it to this degree before in my life. And I’ve talked to a lot of people that are a lot older than me and they say they’ve never seen anything. Because the Bible talks about pestilence, it talks about famines, it talks about earthquakes, it talks about all this kind of — and we’re © Fillius Jazz Archive -15-

having all this stuff right while we speak. So from a spiritual standpoint, and I’m a believer in eternity and that kind of stuff. So it’s just kind of pointing to what is going to happen in the future. And that’s just my personal opinion. I talk to my students sometimes, of course you don’t want to talk religion too much at school. I kind of keep away from that. But basically they have no use for it at all. A lot of them don’t. Because they’ve seen the hypocrisy from parents and, you know from other people of if you’re a believer in Christ what Christ would do versus what you see. And one thing that really does get me angry is the Evangelical right and the embracement of a guy that has no moral background too much at all. And I’m just speaking — this is just me talking. And they are, it’s like the Pharisees of old, they killed Jesus and some people were looking the other way. As long as you can get your agenda taken care of, we don’t care. And that (A) drives me nuts.
It drives me nuts too. And I guess sometimes people say well it’s all about as long as they get the conservative judges they want or something, but that seems like a poor excuse to me.

It’s a real poor excuse and young people see that phoniness and they don’t want to have any part of it. And that’s the thing, it really bothers me. If something gets me angry, that gets me angry more than anything else. And now we don’t know how the election is going to turn out. I’m going to go vote early, and I’m going to do my little two cents, because that’s all you can do. But you know what I try to do my classes and we talk about it and I say, “You guys go out and vote.” See the last time the young people didn’t vote. And they’ve got to go out and vote. You’re seeing all this unrest, but the beautiful thing, especially about the racial unrest, is the joining of African-Americans and white Americans, and all nat— it’s a beautiful sight. When Dr. King did his speech in sixty— you didn’t see that. But today, I mean it’s just a beautiful rainbow of people out there that are all stripes, and to me that what this country is all about.
